settings.title: Settings
settings.agentLead: Any AI app that speaks MCP can work in the studio. Add it once; it follows the open project.
settings.agentHow: After adding it, start the AI and ask it to call start_here. The dot in the top bar turns violet when it is connected.
settings.noProject: No project is open, so there is nothing to check yet. Open one in Projects.
settings.waiting: {name} is open, but no agent has called in for a minute.
settings.packageLead: The studio as it stands, in one zip, to try on another machine or with another agent. Your projects are not in it.
settings.package: Download the studio as a zip
splash.offline: The studio is not running. Start it with Start Studio; this window connects by itself.
hub.sampleLead: Each opens as a copy, so you can ask for changes freely.
ref.warn.moreVideos: The page holds {count} videos; only the first was saved.
ref.warn.fpsUnknown: ffmpeg is not installed, so the frame rate of this file was not read.
ref.warn.lowFps: The source is {fps} fps, so measured timing is less exact than a 60 fps recording.
ref.warn.probeFailed: The file was saved, but ffmpeg could not read it ({reason}).
ref.fail.badLink: This is not a link the studio can use. Paste the address of the video's own page (https).
ref.fail.badArgument: The start and end of the part must be numbers of seconds, with the start before the end.
ref.fail.busy: Another download is still running for this project. Wait for it to finish, then paste the next link.
ref.fail.noYtDlp: Saving a video from a link needs the yt-dlp program, which is not installed here. Install it (Windows: winget install yt-dlp), then restart the studio.
ref.fail.noFfmpeg: Saving part of a video needs ffmpeg, which is not installed here. Install ffmpeg, or save the whole video.
ref.fail.timeout: The site did not answer in time, or the download took too long and was stopped. Try once more later, or a shorter part.
ref.fail.badContainer: The video came in a file type the studio cannot read. Save the video another way and add it as a file.
ref.fail.downloadFailed: The program finished but no video file was saved. A video over the size limit is the most likely cause; add a shorter recording as a file.
ref.fail.botCheck: The site asked for a sign-in to prove this is not a bot. Wait 15-30 minutes before trying again. The studio never uses your browser cookies, so you can also download the video yourself and add the file.
ref.fail.rateLimited: The site is limiting requests from this computer. Wait 15-30 minutes before trying again; do not retry in a loop.
ref.fail.tooLarge: This video is larger than the 300 MB limit. Add a shorter recording as a file.
ref.fail.unavailable: This video cannot be downloaded without signing in: it is private, members-only, removed, or blocked by age or region. Add a recording of it as a file instead.
ref.fail.unsupportedSite: The yt-dlp program found no video it can read at that address. Paste the address of the video's own page, or save the video another way and add it as a file.
ref.fail.loginRequired: This site only shows the video to a signed-in account. The studio never signs in and never uses your browser cookies. Save the video another way and add it as a file.
ref.fail.notFound: There is no video at that address (the page is gone or the link is wrong). Check the link.
ref.fail.blocked: The site refused the request (it wants a sign-in or blocks this program). Save the video another way and add it as a file.
ref.fail.network: The download failed on the network. Check the connection and try once more.
ref.fail.unknown: The download failed for a reason the studio does not recognise.
settings.addonsLead: Optional programs. The studio works without them; each one adds a single ability. Restart the studio after installing one.
settings.addon.ffmpeg: Reads reference videos: the filmstrip, measuring a move, comparing with the result, and saving part of a video.
settings.addon.ytdlp: Saves a video from a link (YouTube or a public video page) into the project's reference folder. The link field appears beside the reference when it is installed.
settings.addon.spineCli: Lets an agent ask the real Spine editor whether a file opens (needs a Spine license). Every other check works without it.
settings.spineLead: The studio plays and writes animation on its own engine; Spine 4.2 JSON files open and save without this add-on. The add-on brings Esoteric Software's official Spine runtime for what the engine does not do yet: physics, transform and path constraints, binary .skel files, and the official runtime's verdict beside the studio's.
settings.spineLicense: The official runtime is not part of Keyframe Studio. It is under the Spine Runtimes License: you need your own Spine Editor license to use it. When you turn the add-on on, the studio downloads it from Esoteric Software's npm package into this computer's app data; turning it off deletes it.
settings.spineAccept: I have my own Spine license and accept the Spine Runtimes License.
settings.spineInstalled: The Spine add-on is on. Reload the page to use the official player on the stage.
settings.spineRemoved: The Spine add-on is off and its files are deleted.
settings.themeLead: Dark keeps the stage calm; light suits bright rooms.
settings.languageLead: The studio's own words. Your AI answers in the language you write in.

chat.suggest.bounceText: Give it more bounce: a bigger overshoot before it settles.
chat.suggest.loopText: Make it loop: the last frame should lead back into the first.
first.title: Describe it. Watch it move.
first.lead: Keyframe Studio is where your AI animates. You say what should move and how; the AI writes the animation; the studio plays it, checks it and saves it beside your file. Your own file is never changed.
first.connectLead: Add the studio to your AI once. The dot turns violet when the studio hears from it.
first.directorLead: The easiest way: the studio's own Director. It runs Claude Code from the chat here, with nothing to set up; you only need it installed and signed in once.
first.directorMissing: Claude Code was not found on this computer. Install it with {install}, then run {signIn} once to sign in.
first.mcp: Or connect any MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code…)
first.waiting: Waiting for an AI to connect…
first.open: Open an example, or your own folder
first.describeLead: “Make her wave twice, the second one bigger.” The AI writes it, the studio checks it, and it plays on the stage.

settings.whereClaude: Run this once in a terminal. It adds the studio to Claude Code in every folder; then start claude and ask it to call start_here.
settings.whereOther: Add this to the app's MCP settings. Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Claude Desktop and most others take this same block.
connect.desktopDone: Added. Quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again; the studio's tools then show there. Your earlier config was saved as {backup}.
connect.desktopAdded: Claude Desktop has the studio. If its tools do not show, quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again.
connect.desktopOld: Claude Desktop has an older entry for the studio: press Add again to update it.
connect.desktopMissing: Claude Desktop was not found on this computer. Install it from claude.ai/download and open it once.
connect.whereDesktop: One click adds the studio to Claude Desktop, keeping your other servers and a backup of the file. Or paste this into Claude Desktop > Settings > Developer > Edit Config yourself.
connect.scope: The AI works only through the studio's tools, on the project open here. It runs on your own AI account, and its usage is billed there.
update.title: Updates
update.auto: Check for a new version when the studio starts
update.installed: {version} is installed: restart to use it
update.ready: Installed. Your projects and settings stay where they are. Restart when you are ready.

settings.aboutLead: Runs on this computer only. Nothing about you or your projects is sent anywhere; the app only asks whether a new version is out, and you can turn that off.
agent.roleLead.director: Talks with you and writes the animation.
agent.roleLead.art-director: Draws, keeps the style guide and checks the art when the Director asks.
agent.roleLead.senior-animator: Writes and polishes motion when the Director asks.
agent.roleLead.researcher: Finds references and timings for the Director.
agent.briefPlaceholder.art-director: e.g. Clean shapes, no heavy outlines, the project's palette.
agent.briefPlaceholder.senior-animator: e.g. Snappy timing, strong anticipation, keep the feet planted.
agent.briefPlaceholder.researcher: e.g. Look for real footage first and note the frame counts.
